title: KCNH1 variants associated with neurodevelopmental disorders exhibit prominent gain of function
title_zh: KCNH1 变异与神经发育障碍相关，表现出显著的功能增强
abstract: Abstract Pathogenic variants in KCNH1, encoding the human ether-á-go-go voltage-gated potassium channel (EAG1, KV10.1), are associated with the neurodevelopmental disorders Temple-Baraitser syndrome (TBS), Zimmermann-Laband syndrome (ZLS), epileptic encephalopathy, and other undefined neurodevelopmental disorders. Investigating the functional consequences of KCNH1 variants can provide information about molecular and cellular pathophysiological mechanisms and help guide therapeutic directions. In this study, we determined the functional properties of 26 disease-associated KCNH1 variants including three recurrent and six that were previously unpublished. Findings were compared to the wildtype (WT) channel along with six rare population variants. Our approach used automated patch clamp recording of heterologously expressed KCNH1 variants in both the homozygous state (variant alone) and the clinically-relevant heterozygous state (variant co-expressed with WT channels). We also examined the impact of alternative splice isoforms on functional consequences of specific variants. We demonstrated that the majority of disease-associated KCNH1 variants exhibit features consistent with gain-of-function including hyperpolarized voltage-dependence of activation, accelerated activation kinetics, or both that promote hyperpolarization of the resting membrane potential. By contrast, one unique variant discovered previously in an autism cohort had a depolarized voltage-dependence of activation and was associated with a depolarized resting potential in cells. Pharmacological testing of KCNH1 variants demonstrated differences in potency for channel block by imipramine and an investigational non-selective potassium channel blocker (LY97241) for specific variants. Collectively, our findings support gain-of-function as the most common, albeit not exclusive, molecular mechanism underlying KCNH1-related disorders and suggest opportunities for potential therapeutic drug repurposing strategies for these conditions.
abstract_zh: 摘要：KCNH1基因编码人类以太-阿戈-戈电压门控钾通道（EAG1，KV10.1）的突变与Temple-Baraitser综合征（TBS）、Zimmermann-Laband综合征（ZLS）、癫痫性脑病及其他未定义的神经发育障碍相关。研究KCNH1变异的功能后果可揭示分子与细胞层面的病理机制，并指导治疗方向。本研究测定了26种与疾病相关的KCNH1变异的功能特性，其中包括三种重复变异和六种此前未公开的变异。结果与野生型（WT）通道以及六种罕见人群变异进行比较。我们采用自动化贴片钳技术记录异源表达的KCNH1变异在纯合状态（仅变异）和临床相关的杂合状态（变异与WT通道共表达）下的电生理特征，并评估可变剪接亚型对特定变异功能影响。结果显示，大多数疾病相关的KCNH1变异表现出功能增强的特征，包括激活电位的超极化依赖性、激活动力学加速或两者兼有，从而促进静息膜电位的超极化。相反，在自闭症人群中发现的一个独特变异表现出激活电位的去极化依赖性，并与细胞静息电位的去极化相关。对KCNH1变异进行药理学测试，发现不同变异对咪氯美辛和一种正在研发的非选择性钾通道阻滞剂（LY97241）的通道阻断效力存在差异。综上所述，我们的发现支持功能增强是KCNH1相关疾病最常见的分子机制，尽管并非唯一机制，并提示针对这些疾病的潜在药物再利用策略。
